full_judgment:
In the above noted suit the petitioner, as plaintiff No.1 and his brother Abul Kashem as Plaintiff No. 2, prayed for a decree of recovery of possession of the suit land under section 9 of the Act, 1877. The suit land has been described in the schedule to the plaint along with a sketch map. It measures 6 decimals out of 31 decimals of Plot No. 388, appertaining to CS Khatian No. 45 corresponding to ROR Khatian No. 63, Mutation Khatian Nos. 231 and 343. The land has further been described with reference to the boundary holders on the four sides. 

 3. The plaintiffs claim that the suit plot No. 388 and three other plots including plot No. 389 were recorded in CS Khatian No. 45 in the name of Soleman Sheikh, who by a Heba deed dated 6-11-1939 gifted 27 decimals of land out of 95 decimals of the four CS plots to his two sisters Azifat Nessa and Ata Nessa. By amicable partition, Azifat Nessa used to possess 25 cents, being 17 cents in plot 388 and 8 cents in plot No. 389. 

 4. Subsequently the ROR khatian was prepared in the names of Azifat Nessa and her three brothers Mia Chan, Dengu and Shahed Ali. On the death of Azifat Nessa her share, being 25 cents, devolved upon four sons named Mohor Ali Munshi, Abdul Sheikh, Surjit and Abu Sheikh and two daughters named Jaigun and Amena. 

 28. It may be noted that the plaintiffs produced a document purporting to be the certified copy of the ROR. Khatian No. 63 and it has been marked as Exhibit 1(Ka) But PW 6, being an employee of the District Record Room, produced the concerned original volume. He stated that the entries of the volume with regard to ROR Khatian No. 63 do not fully tally with the said purported true copy and that it was not issued from his office. 

 30. From the evidence on record I hold that the plaintiffs may have some subsisting interest in suit Khatian as co-sharer. But their exclusive possession over the suit land as claimed in the schedule to the plaint and dispossession there-from could not be proved by credible evidence for the purpose of obtaining a decree under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877.
